_meta.source: SYNTHESISED to the real system.vessels/system.bodies wire shape (Gonogo.KSP/KspHost.cs BuildVesselRosterEntry -> Sitrep.Host/SystemViewProvider.cs BuildSystemVessels), values checked against Assembly-CSharp.dll (ilspycmd decompile, KSP_Data/Managed): Vessel.GetCrewCount/GetCrewCapacity, ProtoVessel.GetVesselCrew, ProtoPartSnapshot.partPrefab.CrewCapacity, CommNet.CommNetVessel.OnStart/GetControlLevel. Seven vessels covering every roster state an operator actually sees: direct link (station), relay link (probe/lander), a real no-link reading (orbiter -- CommNet resolved and reports None, a genuine ops fact), a real debris entry (crewCount/crewCapacity are honest zeros -- Part.CrewCapacity sums to 0 for a debris part, not an unknown -- but commsConnected/commsControlSource are omitted because CommNetVessel.OnStart never attaches a CommNet node to VesselType.Debris at all: this is the vessel type's permanent by-design state, not a glitch), an asteroid entry for the same structural reason (VesselType.SpaceObject is excluded by the identical OnStart guard), and one genuinely-unresolved entry (every field omitted -- the producer's own transient 'nothing to read this tick' case: a scene-transition race or a vessel whose protoVessel/connection hasn't settled yet, NOT what a stable debris/asteroid vessel looks like). There is no reliability/health signal behind any entry - this widget does not compute a per-vessel status.
